_comment: Why this release declares the rollback policy it does. Required when the policy is backup-required, because that declaration costs a site an emergency database restore to recover from any failed activation, and nothing else makes anyone justify it: verify-rollback-compatibility.sh short-circuits on backup-required and asks for no evidence, while service-compatible must ship a digest-matched proof. The heavier claim was the cheaper one to make, so it was inherited by copying the row forward.
justification: Conservative rather than assessed. 1.4.15 adds no migration, but it changes who may write a chart (a phone watching a case another device holds writes nothing) and how planned changes are entered, and no release-specific rollback proof shows 1.4.14 services behaving correctly on charts written by 1.4.15. Declaring service-compatible would be an unverified claim, so rolling back stays tied to the verified pre-update backup.
